prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S314: The Regional Flow Platform marks a proposed Target Off Block Time as conditional when the required handling resources are forecast to arrive after the aircraft ready time.
S315: The Departure Metering Service can absorb a small ground handling variation, but repeated slips from multiple stands reduce confidence in the planned departure stream.
S316: The Aircraft Operator Representative is expected to declare whether the operator can accept a later off-block time without causing crew, connection, or aircraft rotation impacts.
S317: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the same information to decide whether a swap between company flights is operationally meaningful or merely transfers a handling bottleneck to another stand.
S318: In Normal Operations, the system assumes that typical service durations remain valid unless the Handling Resource Planner reports a constraint or the stand status stops advancing.
S319: During Adverse Weather Mode, bus turn times, loader movements, and tow availability are padded because apron driving speeds fall and personnel may be redeployed to safety duties.
S320: In the Recovery Phase, the system does not release every aircraft as soon as it becomes ready because a surge of simultaneous pushbacks can exceed tow team availability and block service roads.
S321: Each resource-driven revision is recorded in the Collaborative Decision Log with the reason code, revised Target Off Block Time, and affected flight identifier.
S322: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares predicted and actual handling constraints to improve standard service times and to identify chronic equipment shortages by stand group.
S323: Airspace restrictions are managed as tactical constraints that affect sector capacity, arrival acceptance, departure release timing, and the sequencing assumptions used by the Meridian regional operation.
S324: Military coordination is led through scheduled planning calls and short-notice coordination channels so that civil traffic managers receive usable timing, altitude, and boundary information before a constraint becomes active.
S325: The Military Airspace Liaison sends the Temporary Restriction Notice after confirming the activation window, affected volume, controlling authority, and any published contingency conditions.
S326: The Airspace Sector Planner converts confirmed restricted area information into sector availability assumptions and checks whether existing flight plans require rerouting, metering, or ground delay action.
S327: When a temporary restricted area reduces usable route options, the Regional Flow Manager assesses whether the effect is localized to one stream or requires a broader Ground Delay Program.
S328: The Capacity Assessment Module treats a restriction as a time-bounded reduction in route, sector, or airport throughput, depending on the geometry and operational impact of the area.
